resources.string: Updates come from your contacts, over Tor, with no server. Each version is signed by the developer: Whospair checks the signature before downloading, then the file against it, and Android checks that it is signed with the same key as the app you have. A modified app is always refused.
Version %1$s (%2$s) is offered by one of your contacts. It downloads while Whospair is open; if the connection drops, it resumes where it stopped.
Android must first allow Whospair to install updates. Allow it, come back, then tap again.
You pass version %1$s on to your confirmed contacts.
This package is not signed by the Whospair developer, or it is damaged. Nothing was installed.
Signature verified. Android will ask you to confirm the installation.
Signature verified. This phone now passes this version on to your confirmed contacts.
This is your version, but the app installed here is not the same file. Nothing to pass on.
This package is older than your version. Nothing was installed.
Not enough memory to download it.
The file received does not match the signature. It was discarded.
This version is not signed with the same key as your app. Refused.
Source unreachable, new attempt in 10 s
A newer version of Whospair has been available for more than 5 days. Install it to keep using the app: your up-to-date contacts no longer accept older versions.
Update interrupted, new attempt in 30 min
